sources.citation: Wright, Jennifer. 2012. Testing and Revising a Tone Orthography Proposal for Chrambo (Bambalang). Yaoundé: SIL Cameroon. 39 pp.
sources.note: Nothing; states noun roots carry one of four whole-word tone patterns H, L, HL, LH (after Luider 2009).

sources.citation: Luider, Jennifer. 2009. A Phonological Sketch of the Bambalang (Chrambo) Language. Yaoundé: SIL Cameroon. 43 pp.
sources.note: Nothing: no stress/accent section and the words stress/accent/prominence do not occur. Sec. 6 'Lexical tone' (p.34-40): four tones H, L, HL, LH on syllables in isolation, mid only via downstep; noun and verb tone patterns by syllable shape. p.41: utterance-level tone and intonation explicitly not examined.

sources.citation: Fozoh, Ayafor Vera Mapi. 2002. The structural phonology of Círàmbɔ. MA thesis, Dept. of African Languages and Linguistics, Université de Yaoundé I. viii+95 pp.
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Ch. 2 'Tones' p.11: 'Círàmbɔ as an African language and especially a Bantu language manifests tone, so it is a tone language'; inventory of five surface tones (H, M, L, rising, falling), tonal processes; ch. 5 syllable/word structure (V, CV, CVV, CVC, C syllables) with no mention of stress or accent.
